newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch 1996 GDP growth revised upwards to 3.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Dutch 1996 GDP growth revised upwards to 3.3 pct.

text.p: Dutch gross domestic product (GDP) growth for the year 1996 was revised upwards to 3.3 percent from a previous estimate of 2.7 percent, the Central Bureau of Statistics said on Tuesday.
A spokesman for the bureau said the current figure was based on the national accounts for 1996, whereas previous figures were based on quarterly accounts.

It added that the rise in 1996 was the strongest since 1990. The strong rise was caused in particular by hefty increases in consumer spending and investments by companies in buildings, machinery and other fixed assets.
Consumer spending growth for the full year 1996 was revised upwards to 3.0 percent, compared with a previous estimate of 2.9 percent.
The increase of business investments was now calculated at 6.5 percent, up from a previous estimated rise of 5.8 percent.
